/-!
# Erdős Problem 868

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/868](https://www.erdosproblems.com/868)
- [LaLa26] Larsen and Larsen, [Erdős problem 868](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/blob/main/868.pdf) (2026)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos868

/-- The number of ways in which a natural `n` can be written as the sum of
`o` members of the set `A`. -/
noncomputable
def ncard_add_repr (A : Set ℕ) (o : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  { a : Fin o → ℕ | Set.range a ⊆ A ∧ ∑ i, a i = n }.ncard

/-- Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then
must $A$ contain a minimal additive basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] answered this in the negative.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.parts.i :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ncard_add_repr A 2 n) atTop → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Let $A$ be an additive basis of order $2$, let $f(n)$ denote the number of ways in which
$n$ can be written as the sum of two elements from $A$. If $f(n) > \epsilon \log n$ for large $n$
and an arbitrary fixed $\epsilon > 0$, then must $A$ contain a minimal additive
basis of order $2$?

Larsen and Larsen [LaLa26] constructed a counterexample with $f(n) > c \log n$ for all large $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.parts.ii :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (A : Set ℕ) (ε > 0), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ε * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős and Nathanson proved that this is true if $f(n) > (\log \frac{4}{3})^{-1} \log n$ for
all large $n$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 →
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹ * Real.log n < ncard_add_repr A 2 n) → ∃ B ⊆ A,
      B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧ ∀ b ∈ B, ¬(B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2 := by
  sorry

/-- Härtter and Nathanson proved that there exist additive bases which do not contain
any minimal additive bases. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/hjyuh/formal-conjectures/blob/e0da6ec78953b17618895a093d4bee90fd3f6f67/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/868.lean#L132"]
theorem erdos_868.variants.Hartter_Nathanson (o : ℕ) (ho : 1 < o) : ∃ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o ∧ ∀ B ⊆ A, B.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o →
    ∃ b ∈ B, (B \ {b}).IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder o := by
  sorry

end Erdos868

findings.description: The helper counts ordered tuples, whereas the source's representation function counts nondecreasing tuples. In order 2 it counts both (a,b) and (b,a) when a ≠ b. Writing F for the Lean count and r for the source count, F(n) = 2r(n) − d(n), where d(n) is the diagonal indicator. This changes the hypothesis of Erdos868.erdos_868.variants.fixed_ε: its numerical coefficient is left unchanged despite the approximately doubled count, giving a stronger assertion than the cited result. A scratch proof establishes ncard_add_repr {1,2} 2 3 = 2, whereas the source count is 1. This convention is harmless in parts (i) and (ii), as recorded under reformulations, but not in the fixed-coefficient variant.
findings.source_evidence: Larsen–Larsen, Robust additive bases without minimal subbases, §1, p. 1, explicitly defines r_A(m) as the number of pairs (a,b) ∈ A² with a+b=m and a≤b: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-868/main/868.pdf. Erdős–Nathanson (1987), p. 90, likewise defines r_h(n) using a₁≤⋯≤a_h: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-25.pdf. The logarithmic theorem uses this unordered representation function.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an unordered count, for example `{a : Fin o → ℕ | Monotone a ∧ Set.range a ⊆ A ∧ ∑ i, a i = n}.ncard`. Alternatively retain the ordered helper but translate the numerical hypothesis accordingly. The missing strict margin in variants.fixed_ε also needs the separate correction below.

findings.description: Line 74 hardcodes C = (Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹ and assumes only that C * log n < f(n) eventually. The cited theorem instead assumes f(n) > c * log n eventually for some fixed c strictly greater than C. Even after correcting the representation count, the Lean statement asserts the endpoint case rather than the published theorem. Strict inequality for each n does not supply a uniform positive margin in the coefficient; integer-valuedness does not fix this distinction. The docstring repeats the same overstatement.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Nathanson, Systems of distinct representatives and minimal bases in additive number theory (1979), Theorem 2, p. 100: “r(n) > c log n for some constant c > log⁻¹(4/3) and all n > N₁.” https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-25.pdf. The introduction of the file's cited Larsen–Larsen paper, p. 1, explicitly repeats the condition c > (log(4/3))⁻¹.
findings.suggested_fix: After using the source-aligned unordered count, quantify over `c : ℝ` with `(Real.log (4 / 3))⁻¹ < c`, and assume `∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, c * Real.log n < unordered_add_repr A 2 n`. Keep the same minimal-subbasis conclusion. Update the docstring to include this strict coefficient condition. This corrected proposition was type-checked in /workspace/review/corrected_statement.lean.

reformulations.difference: The Lean growth condition uses ordered representation counts instead of the source's unordered counts.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every A and n, the unordered count r and ordered count F satisfy r(n) ≤ F(n) ≤ 2r(n). Consequently F tends to infinity if and only if r does. The universal question, and hence its fixed negative answer, is unchanged. The count bounds and the equivalence of the entire universal statements were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The logarithmic question uses ordered counts, but quantifies over all positive coefficients inside the answer statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since r ≤ F ≤ 2r, an eventual bound F(n) > ε log n implies r(n) > (ε/2) log n, and a bound r(n) > ε log n implies the same bound for F. Thus existence of some positive logarithmic lower-bound coefficient is equivalent for the two conventions. Because the conclusion is independent of ε and ε is universally quantified, the entire universal questions are equivalent. This equivalence was proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The source says that A contains no minimal subbasis; Lean says every basis B ⊆ A has a removable element.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The basis property is upward-closed under inclusion. Thus B has a proper subset that remains a basis if and only if B\{b} remains a basis for some b∈B. Negating the existence of a minimal subbasis therefore gives exactly the Lean quantifiers. Both the single-deletion/proper-subset characterization and the logical equivalence were proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: The two findings are independent discrepancies affecting variants.fixed_ε; the counting discrepancy is reported at its defining helper rather than duplicated on the theorem. No claim is made that the stronger Lean theorem has been disproved. Larsen–Larsen Theorem 1 supports the solved/False records for both main parts. The all-orders Hartter_Nathanson statement is supported by the explicit {1} ∪ hℕ example in Erdős–Nathanson (1987). Scratch checks compiled without errors or sorry, establishing finiteness of all representation sets, boundary cases, the count-convention equivalences, and the minimality characterization. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/868 returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its live remarks/status could not be independently inspected; the cited solution and original literature were used instead. The external formal_proof attribution was not independently validated. The reviewed file's hash remains identical to the committed file.

demonstrated.claim: For A = {1,2}, the imported helper counts two representations of 3, namely (1,2) and (2,1), whereas the source's unordered count is one.

not_demonstrated.reason: The missing strict coefficient margin does not provide a trivial proof or disproof of the actual additive-basis statement; no concrete basis counterexample has been established here, and an arbitrary growth-sequence example would not demonstrate this declaration.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with a short example using the imported definition directly. The requested compilation completed without errors or warnings.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«868»

/-! A concrete check of the representation-count convention in Erdős 868. -/

-- Erdos868.ncard_add_repr counts 3 = 1 + 2 twice for A = {1,2},
-- whereas the source's unordered count is 1 (only the pair with a ≤ b).
example : Erdos868.ncard_add_repr ({1, 2} : Set ℕ) 2 3 = 2 := by
  rw [Erdos868.ncard_add_repr, Set.ncard_eq_two]
  refine ⟨![1, 2], ![2, 1], by decide, ?_⟩
  ext a
  simp [Set.range_subset_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two, Fin.sum_univ_two, funext_iff]
  omega

submission.summary: Added Monotone to the representation tuples so the helper counts unordered representations while allowing repetitions. Updated the fixed-constant variant to quantify over a real coefficient c strictly greater than (log(4/3))⁻¹ and use c in the eventual logarithmic bound. Updated both docstrings; unrelated declarations and attributes remain unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the existing declaration-uses-sorry warnings.
